cds.text: Recognise, represent and order numbers to at least 1000
Partition, rearrange and regroup two- and three-digit numbers; recognise the role of zero in place value
Recognise one-half as one of 2 equal parts; connect halves, quarters and eighths by repeated halving
Add and subtract one- and two-digit numbers using number sentences and part-part-whole reasoning
Multiply and divide by one-digit numbers using repeated addition, equal grouping, arrays and partitioning
Model practical additive and multiplicative problems, including money, and interpret the solutions
Recognise, represent and order natural numbers beyond 10 000
Recognise and represent unit fractions and their multiples; combine fractions with the same denominator
Add and subtract two- and three-digit numbers without a calculator, using place value
Multiply and divide one- and two-digit numbers using number sentences, diagrams and arrays
Estimate quantities in collections and use estimates to check problem-solving calculations
Model additive and multiplicative problems, including financial contexts, and interpret the solutions
Follow and create algorithms with steps and decisions to investigate numbers; describe patterns
Recognise and extend place value to tenths and hundredths; name and represent decimals
Explain and use the properties of odd and even numbers
Find equivalent fractions using related denominators; connect fractions and decimal notation
Count by fractions, including mixed numerals; locate them on number lines
Solve problems multiplying or dividing natural numbers by multiples and powers of 10
Develop efficient strategies and use digital tools for addition, subtraction, multiplication and division
Use estimation and rounding to check and explain the reasonableness of calculations
Model additive and multiplicative problems, including financial contexts, using number sentences
Follow and create algorithms using addition or multiplication to generate sets of numbers; describe patterns

sentences.text: {{S}} works confidently with large numbers, reads and writes values in the millions, and understands decimals to the hundredths and thousandths.
{{S}} confidently works with large numbers and applies place value knowledge to understand numbers in the millions.
{{S}} compares and orders decimals and percentages.
{{S}} works confidently with large numbers in the millions and applies place value to solve a range of problems.
{{S}} compares and orders whole numbers and fractions and rounds decimals accurately.
{{S}} applies {{pos}} knowledge of place value to work confidently with large numbers.
{{S}} works confidently with large numbers and applies place value to solve problems.
{{S}} rounds whole numbers and decimals to estimate results.
{{S}} reads and represents numbers using place value knowledge.
{{S}} uses place value to read, write and work with large numbers and represents them in different ways.
{{S}} reads, writes, and interprets numbers in a variety of ways.
{{S}} works with whole numbers and applies place value to solve problems.
{{S}} rounds numbers to estimate results and records numbers in different ways.
{{S}} is learning to read and represent numbers in different ways and can order numbers up to four digits.
{{S}} separates numbers into groups of tens and ones.
{{S}} counts forwards and backwards from 40.
{{S}} knows one more and one less of numbers up to 100.
{{S}} counts forwards from any given number up to 120.
{{S}} reads, writes and orders three-digit numbers.
{{S}} states what each digit is worth in a three-digit number.
{{S}} identifies the number before and after a given three-digit number.
{{S}} understands that one thousand is made up of ten hundreds and represents numbers using words and drawings.
{{S}} arranges numbers of up to six digits from lowest to highest.
{{S}} applies a range of addition and subtraction strategies effectively.
{{S}} applies known strategies to solve addition and subtraction problems.
{{S}} uses {{pos}} knowledge of addition and subtraction to solve complex worded problems.
{{S}} applies different strategies to solve addition and subtraction problems.
{{S}} uses known number facts and basic strategies to solve addition and subtraction problems.
{{S}} solves subtraction with three-digit numbers.
{{S}} solves simple addition problems by doubling, such as '6 and 6 makes 12'.
{{S}} uses taught strategies to solve addition and subtraction problems with combinations up to 20.
{{S}} uses concrete materials to model addition and subtraction problems involving two-digit numbers.
{{S}} uses the equals sign to show when two number sentences have the same total.
{{S}} recalls related addition and subtraction facts for numbers to at least 20.
{{S}} solves addition and subtraction problems by separating numbers into their place value.
{{S}} solves addition and subtraction problems using appropriate mental strategies.
{{S}} uses estimation to decide whether an answer is reasonable.
{{S}} solves addition and subtraction problems with numbers of any size using a range of strategies.
{{S}} multiplies and divides decimals accurately and works through calculations with several steps in the correct order.
{{S}} multiplies 2- and 3-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers and represents and solves division problems with whole number remainders.
{{S}} recalls multiplication facts to support calculations and solves division problems with remainders.
{{S}} creates number patterns using known multiplication facts.
{{S}} generates number patterns using times tables.
{{S}} solves division problems with whole number remainders.
{{S}} recalls some multiplication facts and uses them to support calculations.
{{S}} counts by twos, threes and fives to recognise simple division and creates equal groups to show multiplication.
{{S}} uses visual representations to find multiplication facts.
{{S}} uses strategies to solve simple division problems.
{{S}} models and describes collections of objects as 'groups of', such as two groups of three.
{{S}} recognises and continues number patterns that increase by twos, fives, and tens past 100.
{{S}} organises objects into equal rows and columns as part of {{pos}} multiplication knowledge.
{{S}} has developed {{pos}} understanding of related multiplication and division facts.
{{S}} recognises that multiplication and division are opposites and uses one to solve the other.
{{S}} recognises that doubling a number gives the same answer as multiplying by 2.
{{S}} recalls multiplication facts up to 10 × 10 and uses them to solve worded problems.
{{S}} uses number properties, such as swapping the order of numbers, to work out related multiplication facts.
{{S}} compares and orders fractions, decimals and percentages and explains how they are related.
{{S}} calculates percentage discounts and finds fractions of whole numbers.
{{S}} adds and subtracts simple fractions with accuracy.
{{S}} works with fractions and decimals and identifies prime numbers.
{{S}} demonstrates an understanding of the connection between common fractions, decimals and percentages.
{{S}} expresses common percentages as both fractions and decimals.
{{S}} works with fractions and decimals with growing accuracy.
{{S}} understands common fractions and writes them as decimals.
{{S}} recognises and represents fractions of a length and records numbers in different forms.
{{S}} recognises fractions and decimals and applies them in simple problems.
{{S}} recognises simple fractions such as halves and quarters and records numbers as decimals.
{{S}} converts simple fractions to decimals.
{{S}} represents fractions with halves, quarters and thirds.
{{S}} accurately represents fractions on a number line.
{{S}} writes tenths and hundredths as decimal numbers.
{{S}} represents common fractions using models and number lines.
{{S}} recognises and names simple fractions such as halves and quarters.
{{S}} is learning to recognise, name and represent simple fractions.
{{S}} models halves, quarters, and eighths of a collection using counters.
{{S}} divides objects into equal halves, quarters and eighths to represent fractions.
{{S}} shows that different fractions can represent the same amount.
